You know that feeling you get when you're playing a MMORPG and some rich, greedy and childish person comes over to your freshly born character and just destroys your little armour and weapons with their legendary sword of shining muffin whatever? I do, I know that feeling. I bet a lot of people do. I have rage quitted on so many online games because the balance between new people, good people with no money, great people with no money and people with money that are cruel to those who just joined, is so unequal and poisoned there is more chance to meet someone in no man's sky than to get anywhere in a game like that.
Not this game. TESO is so diverse and equal to all its players that it doesn't make a difference if you have the all the dlc's or the premium membership because the only way you can get great stuff, is by your own effort. And even then it's forgiving to new players, as long as you understand the combat system and enemy attacks you will probably get rather far quite quickly. And when you complete a mission -Oh is it satisfying- You actually feel like you have earned something, like what you did was worthwhile. You didn't get some measly axe from whiterun that is so weak your steel weapon is better - no, you got a cleaver that will make a difference to that mission you are struggling with.
You got to level ten? Oh don't you feel proud of yourself! You aren't just measly noob material, you're slightly above that AND you unlocked something! Trying to be a certain character type without having to level up ridiculously quick so that you can get that skill you want? Just go out looking skills are EVERYWHERE!
TESO is probably the best MMORPG I have ever played. It is kind and equal to you like a loving mother is to her two children. It is just challenging enough for you to get that adrenaline without rage quitting. You feel like you got somewhere every time you finish a mission. You don't feel small or threatened by bigger players. You don't get killed by others the second you go on! It's like TES and real life had a love child, TES took the child and raised it to be fair and equal unlike real life, yet it gained the beautiful looks of real life!

After playing this game for a few hours and reliving the nostalgia of my childhood I'd have to say that the game definitely delivered. However! There are a few bugs or irritations (namely 2 during my playthrough) that should be prioritized for a fix above all else if I'm to call it the "closest to perfect" remaster and that is to recalibrate the formations so that they actually have a meaning in the game. There have been so many instances (practically the whole game) where formations didn't decide the flow of battle. The units just scattered in combat and thus left a lot of undeserved casualties.
The second thing to fix is the AI for the harvesters. In the original you could send them out to do their business and wouldn't need to worry about them unless being attacked. But after finishing the first nebula mission and sending them to harvest the rest of the area, they went out, took care of one vein and then just went stationary like there wasn't any resources left (but of course there still were). So I had to manually send them to another vein and have them continue.
These need to be fixed if it is to be remembered fully to the original. Many things have been done great but there are still a few things that just ruin the game for me.
Overall it is of course a beautiful remaster of the game and the graphics are set on. Just needs a bit of fixing but since it just released I can definitely give the developers some time.

I find it rather depressing that I find the complete version of this game and the eventual remasters of Blue Shift and Opposing Force to be more appealing than any other AAA title being released this year or the next with the exception of something like Metro: Exodus.  But I digress: this game is an absolute masterpiece in terms of visuals and just how much it builds upon the original.  Valve, please let these guys make HL3... or HL4 if you're feeling so sensitive about the number three.  Also, just to inform the reader, I'll be reviewing the singleplayer only.  I haven't really touched the multiplayer all that much.
Pros:
-A glamorous revision of the original Half-Life.  Areas are bigger with updated textures and a side of a few additional rooms that weren't there prior.  I'm sure you'd find some issues with the textures if you looked closely enough, but I don't believe you'll care enough to stop and look unless you're trying to read the post-it notes and writing on the whiteboards.
-Well voice acted.  In addition to finding VAs who sound like the original characters like Kleiner, Barney, and Eli (to a lesser extent), the writting does surpass the original in some places. (E.g, "Though if it's one thing I know for sure is that this guy's been killing marines." instead of "Though if it's one thing I know for sure is that he's been killing my buddies.") Finally, the quality is slightly above HL2 quality where it actually sounds like there's some life and emotion to it.
-While somewhat used sparsely, the soundtrack is well conducted.  Once again, only expect it during major setpieces and for it to barely resemble the original soundtrack with the exceptions of Nuclear Mission Jam, the intro theme, and a few others.
-The suit functions are faithful to their depiction in Half-Life, meaning the flash light and sprint aren't tied to the same power source.
-Weapons are as they were with new sounds and idle animations.  While the crossbow and revolver have full-on iron sights now, there's always the option to turn that off.
-The combat is definitely not for the casual audience.  If you want to reach the end, you better pay attention and learn to play.  Basically, if you somehow found HL2 difficult, you'll go back to HL2 and find it a cakewalk.
-The usual nooks and crannies with goodies to keep you supplied and going.
-Use of the Steam community workshop.  Yes, it's rather trivial, but it's fun to mess around with the game like that.
-Nostalgia.  Duh.
Cons:
-Still a WIP.  There's a few bugs here and there, and the entirety of Xen is non-existent on the Steam version, having been pushed back till December from last summer by the time this is written.
-
-This is really meant for medium range computers and above, meaning if you bought some cheap piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥like an HP laptop, you'll need an alternative.
-That ♥♥♥♥ing purple hat. It's a test of your patience, your persistence, and your knowledge of console commands when it boils down to that fight at the portal to Xen during the last chapter at the time of writting.
As a whole, this game gets a 9.5/10
While I know game developers are too stuipid to downsize their budgets to focus more on actual game functionality and subsequently excuse themselves so they can cram in mictrotransactions even in settings where it doesn't make sense, this is the sort of perfection the industry should strive for.

Black Mesa is a fan-made remake of the original Half-Life game. You actually start off with your train leaving a station this time. It seems to be a little longer than in the original game, a little too long, in my opinion. But this time around, the guards and scientists have a lot more models, including… GASP… women!
So quite early in the game, I have already suffered from the wrath of loading screens. They take, like, a minute or longer to load everything. That's what I get for having a crappy laptop. It did get a lot better after the first hour of the game, though.
They’ve added a lot more dialogue for the characters. They actually have, like, real conversations with each other, instead of the nonsensical chatter from the original game. Okay, some of the nonsensical chatter is in here, but only if you have two guys following you.
And of course, among the scientists, you meet with your buddies, Isaac Kleiner and Eli Vance. The two scientists look a lot younger than they do in Half-Life 2. I remember hearing that the events of Half-Life 2 took place 20 after the events of the first game. I don’t know how accurate that is, because I think I only heard it from a mere fan of the franchise, because I haven’t seen anything else confirming it. I actually don’t remember if it was mentioned in the other games. We’ll have to wait until I get to them.
I thought at first that they got the same voice actors from the previous games in here, but it turns out they didn’t. In fact, the voice actors in this game have barely acted in anything else at all, let alone another Half-Life game. I genuinely believed that the original voice actors were in here--except for Eli, because his voice actor is no longer with us. But the voice impressions are pretty spot on.
You don’t get your crowbar in the same spot as the original game, which kinda surprised me. But I’ll be honest, I think it made the game better, especially when you don’t have any other weapon with you. It left me feeling more on edge, being so vulnerable to attacks. But it also filled me with genuine excitement when I actually did find it.
So your first means of defense turns out to be a security guard. Now, the AI of the guards is definitely better than in the original game, but apparently they still haven’t figured out how to step away from danger. And they really love to charge into battle when it’s generally a good idea to NOT.
When you reach the main lobby area, he leaves you alone and tries to call for help. So you are on your own... again… with no weapons… until you get the crowbar, that is.
The graphics are so much better than in Half-Life. Well, duh. They released this game in 2015. That’s like, seventeen years later. They put so much more detail into the objects and environments. Instead of just flat textures on panels and computers, you can actually see the knobs and buttons. And the characters actually look like people.
I love the level design in this game. Every single level is designed differently, or at least has more added to it. When I played this game, it felt like an entirely new experience… except for some areas that are pretty much the same. And some levels are more realistically designed, like some small empty rooms that exist for no reason now being slightly bigger and containing desks and stuff. Some rooms or hallways need to be accessed from a different route than the original. Sometimes you need to go through a vent, and other times you need to solve some sort of puzzle to get through an area. I honestly can’t get enough of these levels.
There are a lot more enemies in this game than there originally were. I guess it’s more realistic to have more soldiers together in one area, but man, the difficulty has gone up. Sometimes it’s batsh** crazy. But I still managed to best them, because I’m Gordon Freeman.
The weapons are slightly different in this game. They’ve completely removed the auto aim, so you have to rely more on yourself to not suck at aiming like I do. And the assault rifle or submachine gun, I’m not sure what it is, can only carry a maximum of three grenades. THREE! In Half-Life, it can hold ten. What are you trying to do, make this less fun? What I also hate is that this particular weapon shares the same ammo as the glock. However much ammo you reload into your pistol is exactly how much less you’ll be able to use for the other gun. Why did they do that? It seems kinda dumb.
The game ends just after you enter the portal that takes you to Xen. Well that kinda sucks. Oh well, I loved this game so far, I’m sure I’ll love Xen just as much.
Now for the ultimate question: Is Black Mesa better than Half-Life? Well, I think it is. Yeah, Half-Life is a classic shooter, and I love it to death, but there are things in this game that I think are improvements compared to the original. Now, I’m not saying that I would choose this game over Half-Life. If I were to suggest a good shooter game, I’d probably point more to the original, because, well, it’s the original. But this game just looks better with it’s better graphics and level design. Feel free to disagree with me, but that’s just how I feel about it.

Based on what I've played so far, I can say that this is a great remake of the original. I won't be spending any more time with it (probably) until the game is complete but this is well worth supporting.
